instruction.text: Which sentence uses the apostrophe (’) correctly? Select the correct answer.
instruction.sound: Which sentence uses the apostrophe correctly? Select the correct answer.

hint.text: Only use a possessive apostrophe when you want to show who, or what, a thing belongs to.

feedback.wrong:
Here are two cats.
“Cats” does not need an apostrophe because it is just plural, not possessive. The sentence is not saying that something belongs to a cat.

This plane has two pilots.
“Pilots” does not need an apostrophe because it is just plural, not possessive. The sentence is not saying that something belongs to a pilot.

b: ++The dog’s bowl is made of metal.

feedback.wrong:
Dogs can be very loyal.
“Dogs” does not need an apostrophe because it is just plural, not possessive. The sentence is not saying that something belongs to a dog.

Michael wears socks with sandals.
“Socks” and “sandals” do not need apostrophes because they are just plural, not possessive. The sentence is not saying that something belongs to socks or sandals.

b: Iris fish tank is very large.
atoms.sound: Irises fish tank is very large.

wrong.text:
Iris’ fish tank is very large.
“Iris” needs an apostrophe because it is possessive. The sentence is saying that the fish tank belongs to Iris.
The name Iris already ends in an s, so you don’t need to add one.
wrong.sound:
Irises fish tank is very large. “Iris” needs an apostrophe because it is possessive. The sentence is saying that the fish tank belongs to Iris.

The name Iris already ends in an s, so you don’t need to add one.

feedback.wrong:
My uncle grows vegetables.
“Vegetables” does not need an apostrophe because it is just plural, not possessive. The sentence is not saying that something belongs to a vegetable.
